openings.claim: Assemble small same-pattern waves by material passes, with the second volunteer checking required quantities while envelopes remain open. The proposed full workflow is unproven.
openings.delta: Replace repeated whole-kit picking and deferred inspection with one quantity rule per pass and correction before closure; shared materials no longer require switching pattern quantities between adjacent envelopes.
openings.prediction: With matched pattern counts, omission rates and crossing reaches should fall without pushing preparation, assembly and checks beyond 90 minutes.
openings.rival_prediction: Nearest alternative: give each volunteer loose local materials while retaining whole-kit assembly. If locality alone explains O4, it should perform equally well; quantity-gated waves should add no accuracy advantage.
openings.defeat: Matched probes show equal or higher omissions with waves, or the smallest useful wave exceeds table space or total elapsed time exceeds 90 minutes.
openings.probe: Compare equal small batches with identical pattern mixes, using existing supplies and the same two volunteers. Keep all materials on the table; record preparation, filling, checking, omissions and reaches. If promising, verify all 60 within the original limits.
assumptions: A useful wave and its supplies fit the existing table.
Small-batch improvements survive the full pattern mix and 60-kit run.

openings.claim: Pencil the assigned pattern name on each envelope before filling and use that identity during checking and distribution; the full-task benefit remains unproven.
openings.delta: Carry pattern identity with the envelope instead of depending on sample consultation or stack position.
openings.prediction: Envelope identity should remain readable after stack mixing, reducing exchanges caused by exterior ambiguity while contents still require independent checking.
openings.rival_prediction: Nearest alternative: separate completed stacks by pattern. This should work while stacks stay separate but lose identity when envelopes become mixed; persistent marks should survive mixing.
openings.defeat: Marked envelopes still cannot be matched correctly to assignments, or marking leads to wrong-pattern contents or breaks the 90-minute limit.
openings.probe: Use existing pencils on six actual envelopes, verify contents against their marks, then have the two volunteers reorder them and recover pattern identity. Include marking time in the subsequent 60-kit timing.
assumptions: Assemblers can access correct participant pattern assignments.
Pattern names are sufficiently distinct and legible.
Marking overhead fits the full 90-minute budget.
